questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode Analysis: What is the output of the following pseudocode?
Integer a = 5, b = 10, c = 2
a = (a + b) / c
If (a > 6)
    b = a * c
Else
    b = a - c
Print b
questions.explanation: a = (5 + 10) / 2 = 15 / 2 = 7 (integer division). Condition (a > 6) evaluates to (7 > 6) which is True. b = a * c = 7 * 2 = 14.

questions.question: Capgemini Game-Based Logic: In a grid path puzzle, a delivery token moves from (0,0) to (3,3). If cell (1,1) and cell (2,2) are blocked obstacles, how many valid shortest paths exist moving only Right and Down?
questions.explanation: Total unconstrained paths = C(6,3) = 20. Paths through (1,1) = C(2,1) * C(4,2) = 2 * 6 = 12. Subtracting blocked paths and accounting for overlap leaves 10 valid paths.

questions.question: A software license at Capgemini is purchased for Rs. 24,000. It depreciates in value by 10% in the first year and 15% in the second year. What is its value at the end of 2 years?
Find the next number in the Capgemini series: 3, 7, 15, 31, 63, ___?

Capgemini Pseudocode: What is the output of the bitwise code?
Integer x = 9, y = 5
Integer z = (x & y) + (x | y)
Print z
questions.explanation: Mathematical identity for any integers: (x & y) + (x | y) = x + y. Here x + y = 9 + 5 = 14.

questions.question: A person completes a project in 18 days working 8 hours a day. In how many days can the same project be completed working 6 hours a day at the same pace?
questions.explanation: Total man-hours = 18 * 8 = 144 hours. At 6 hours/day: days = 144 / 6 = 24 days.

questions.question: Capgemini English: Select the word that correctly replaces the phrase: 'A person who is able to use both hands with equal skill.'
questions.explanation: 'Ambidextrous' is the exact vocabulary term for someone capable of using the right and left hand equally well.

questions.question: If 5 programmers can test 5 modules in 5 minutes, how many minutes will 100 programmers take to test 100 modules?
questions.explanation: 1 programmer tests 1 module in 5 minutes. Therefore, 100 programmers testing 100 modules simultaneously take exactly 5 minutes.

questions.question: A car covers a distance of 450 km in 6 hours. If its speed is increased by 25 km/h, how much time will it take to cover the same distance?
questions.explanation: Initial speed = 450 / 6 = 75 km/h. Increased speed = 75 + 25 = 100 km/h. Time taken = 450 / 100 = 4.5 hours.

questions.question: In how many ways can 6 books on software engineering be arranged on a bookshelf?
questions.explanation: Permutations of 6 items = 6! = 6 * 5 * 4 * 3 * 2 * 1 = 720 ways.

questions.question: Capgemini Deductive Logic: Statements: Some consultants are coders. All coders are innovators. Conclusions: I. Some innovators are coders. II. Some consultants are innovators.
options: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.correct_answer: Both conclusions I and II follow
questions.explanation: Since all coders are innovators, the conversion 'Some innovators are coders' is valid (I). Since some consultants are coders, those consultants are innovators (II). Both follow.

questions.question: A sum invested at simple interest triples itself in 10 years. What is the rate of interest per annum?
questions.explanation: If principal is P, amount is 3P, so SI = 2P. 2P = (P * R * 10)/100 => 2 = R / 10 => R = 20% per annum.

questions.question: What is the probability of drawing an Ace or a King from a well-shuffled standard deck of 52 cards?
questions.explanation: Number of Aces = 4, Kings = 4. Total favorable cards = 8. Probability = 8 / 52 = 2/13.

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode: What is the return value of mystery(3, 4)?
Function mystery(a, b)
    If b == 0 return 1
    Return a * mystery(a, b - 1)
questions.explanation: This is recursive exponentiation: mystery(3, 4) calculates 3^4 = 81.

questions.question: A rectangular server room has length 20 meters and breadth 15 meters. What is the length of the longest cable that can be laid straight across the floor?
questions.explanation: Diagonal = sqrt(20^2 + 15^2) = sqrt(400 + 225) = sqrt(625) = 25 meters.

questions.question: Given an array of integers arr, find the equilibrium index. An equilibrium index is an index such that the sum of elements at lower indexes is equal to the sum of elements at higher indexes. Return -1 if no such index exists.
questions.explanation: Capgemini standard: Compute total sum first; traverse maintaining left_sum; right_sum = total - left_sum - arr[i]. O(N) time and O(1) space.

extra.title: Array Equilibrium Index (Capgemini Exceller)

questions.question: Given two strings text and pattern, return the first index where pattern occurs in text, or -1 if pattern is not part of text. Do not use library indexOf functions.
questions.explanation: Sliding window pattern matching: Compare pattern of length M with substrings of text of length N in O(N*M) or KMP O(N+M).

extra.title: Substring Presence Verification without Built-ins

questions.question: Given an array of integers, count the number of elements that are strictly greater than all previous elements in the array.
questions.explanation: Single pass keeping track of max_so_far. Increment counter whenever arr[i] > max_so_far.

extra.title: Count Elements Greater than All Prior Neighbors

questions.question: Given a binary array nums, return the maximum number of consecutive 1's in the array.
questions.explanation: Iterate through array maintaining current_count of 1s, reset on 0, update max_count.

extra.title: Maximum Consecutive 1's in Binary Array

questions.question: An Arithmetic Progression is an array where the difference between any two consecutive elements is the same. Given an array that represents an AP with exactly one element missing, find the missing element.
questions.explanation: Compute common difference d = (arr[n-1] - arr[0]) / n. Scan array to find where arr[i] - arr[i-1] != d.

extra.title: Missing Number in Arithmetic Progression

questions.question: Given an integer n, return true if it is a power of two. An integer n is a power of two if there exists an integer x such that n == 2^x.
questions.explanation: Bitwise trick: n > 0 && (n & (n - 1)) == 0. A power of two has exactly one set bit.

extra.title: Power of Two Bitwise Check

questions.question: Given a string s consisting of alphabetic characters and spaces, return an array of length 2 where index 0 contains the count of vowels and index 1 contains the count of consonants.
questions.explanation: Normalize to lowercase; check against set of vowels ('a','e','i','o','u') vs alphabetic consonants.

extra.title: Count Vowels and Consonants in a String

questions.question: Given an integer array, compute the total number of element swaps required to sort the array in ascending order using the standard Bubble Sort algorithm.
questions.explanation: Simulate standard bubble sort with adjacent element comparison, incrementing swap counter on each swap.

extra.title: Bubble Sort Swap Count

questions.question: Explain Hexagonal Architecture (Ports and Adapters) and how Capgemini engineering teams utilize it to decouple business core domain logic from external frameworks and databases.
questions.explanation: Hexagonal architecture places application domain logic at the center. Ports define input/output interfaces. Adapters implement concrete infrastructure (REST controller adapter, JPA database adapter), allowing swapping databases or frameworks without touching business logic.

questions.question: How do Java 21 Virtual Threads (Project Loom) differ from traditional platform threads, and what is the underlying carrier thread model?
questions.explanation: Platform threads wrap heavy 1-to-1 OS threads (~1MB stack). Virtual threads are lightweight user-mode threads managed by JVM (~few KB). When a virtual thread executes blocking I/O, JVM unmounts it from the ForkJoinPool carrier thread, freeing carrier threads for other work.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: Explain the Open-Closed Principle (OCP) in SOLID design. How does the Strategy Design Pattern enforce OCP in Capgemini financial payment services?
questions.explanation: Classes should be open for extension, but closed for modification. Strategy pattern defines a PaymentStrategy interface; new payment providers (PayPal, UPI, Card) implement the interface without modifying the core OrderProcessor class.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: What is the difference between SQL Views, Materialized Views, and Stored Procedures? When should an architect avoid business logic in stored procedures?
questions.explanation: Views are saved queries executed on demand. Materialized views persist query results on disk. Stored procedures run procedural code in DB engine. Putting business logic in procedures creates vendor lock-in, poor version control, and difficulties in unit testing.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: Explain Maven Dependency Resolution and how transitive dependency conflicts are resolved using the 'Nearest-Wins' rule and Dependency Exclusions.
questions.explanation: Maven selects the version nearest to the project root in the dependency tree. If conflicting versions exist at the same depth, first declared wins. Developers override using <exclusions> or <dependencyManagement>.

questions.question: How do you implement Distributed Caching with Redis in Spring Boot using the @Cacheable, @CachePut, and @CacheEvict annotations?
questions.explanation: @Cacheable checks Redis cache before method execution. @CachePut updates cache with method return value. @CacheEvict purges stale cache entries on database updates.

questions.explanation: Consumer tests generate a JSON contract (Pact file) specifying expected request and response structures. Provider runs tests verifying that its real endpoints fulfill the contract before deploying.

questions.explanation: Requests pass through a chain of filters (SecurityContextHolderFilter, CsrfFilter, UsernamePasswordAuthenticationFilter). SecurityFilterChain bean configures http.authorizeHttpRequests() and http.oauth2ResourceServer() cleanly using lambda DSL.

questions.question: What is Cursor-Based Pagination versus Offset-Based Pagination in RESTful APIs? Why is cursor pagination preferred for large dataset streaming?
questions.explanation: Offset pagination (OFFSET 10000 LIMIT 20) requires the DB to scan and discard 10,000 rows. Cursor pagination (WHERE id > 10000 LIMIT 20) utilizes indexed B-Trees for O(1) page access and immune to record insertions.

questions.question: How do SonarQube code quality gates enforce Cyclomatic Complexity, Code Smells, and Test Coverage metrics in Capgemini deployment pipelines?
questions.explanation: SonarQube static analysis computes cyclomatic complexity based on decision points (if/for/switch). Quality gates automatically fail CI builds if code coverage < 80% or new blocker vulnerabilities are introduced.

questions.question: Explain the difference between Optimistic Concurrency Control and Pessimistic Concurrency Control in enterprise ERP systems.
questions.explanation: Optimistic concurrency control assumes conflicts are rare, checking a version column on save. Pessimistic concurrency control locks rows at the database level (SELECT FOR UPDATE) preventing any concurrent modification.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: How does Java Garbage Collection work with G1GC (Garbage First Collector), and what does the 'Humongous Allocation' threshold mean?
questions.explanation: G1GC divides heap into equal regions (1MB-32MB). Any object larger than 50% of a region size is classified as a Humongous Object, allocated directly in contiguous Old Gen regions, requiring special handling.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: Explain the Event Sourcing pattern and how it differs from traditional CRUD state storage in audit-sensitive enterprise applications.
questions.explanation: CRUD stores only the current state of an entity. Event Sourcing stores an immutable, append-only log of every domain event that ever occurred, rebuilding current state by replaying events.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: How do you secure containerized microservices running on Docker by enforcing Non-Root Users, Read-Only Root Filesystems, and dropping Linux capabilities?
questions.explanation: Define 'USER appuser' in Dockerfile; run with '--read-only' flag mounting temporary writes to tmpfs; drop all default Linux capabilities with '--cap-drop=ALL' and add only required capabilities.

extra.company_focus: Capgemini 7 Core Values, Hexagonal architecture, clean code principles, Java 17/21 virtual threads (Loom), game-based evaluation

questions.question: What is the difference between Fail-Fast and Fail-Safe iterators in Java Collections framework?
questions.explanation: Fail-Fast iterators (ArrayList, HashMap) throw ConcurrentModificationException if the collection is structurally modified during iteration. Fail-Safe iterators (CopyOnWriteArrayList) operate on a clone, tolerating modifications.

questions.question: How does Capgemini's Generative AI delivery practice accelerate custom software engineering across the software development lifecycle (SDLC)?
questions.explanation: Discuss: AI-assisted requirements drafting, architecture diagram synthesis, code generation, automated regression testing, and code documentation.

questions.question: Explain how Ethical AI frameworks at Capgemini evaluate AI systems against bias, environmental sustainability (Green IT), and regulatory standards.
questions.explanation: Cover: Carbon footprint evaluation of LLM training, algorithmic fairness audits, transparent explanations, and human-in-the-loop accountability.

questions.question: How do you design a RAG architecture to support multilingual technical documentation queries for Capgemini European automotive clients?
questions.explanation: Detail: Multilingual embedding models (e.g. text-embedding-3 or Cohere multilingual), cross-lingual vector search, and language-preserving prompt generation.

questions.question: Describe how AI computer vision models are deployed on edge IoT devices for automated visual defect inspection in manufacturing assembly plants.
questions.explanation: Architecture: High-speed camera captures product images, lightweight YOLO/MobileNet model on edge device (Nvidia Jetson) classifies defects in < 50ms, triggering pneumatic sorting.

questions.question: How do you evaluate and benchmark LLM response quality using LLM-as-a-Judge techniques with automated scoring rubrics at Capgemini?
questions.explanation: Explain: Defining specific criteria (correctness, conciseness, safety), prompting an advanced model with few-shot examples, and checking correlation with human experts.

questions.question: How do you secure proprietary enterprise IP when integrating developer AI coding assistants into Capgemini client project repositories?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Enforcing zero-retention enterprise licenses, prohibiting training on client code, automated scanning for leaked secrets, and strict access controls.

questions.question: Describe how Generative AI can assist in synthesizing realistic test data for enterprise integration testing without exposing real patient/customer PII.
questions.explanation: Detail: Statistical distribution modeling, generative adversarial networks (GANs) or LLMs generating synthetic records adhering to relational database foreign key constraints.

questions.question: How do you design an AI agent workflow using LangGraph or AutoGen where multiple specialized agents collaborate on code refactoring?
questions.explanation: Structure: Analyzer agent identifies code smells, Refactor agent proposes modern Java code, Tester agent executes unit tests, and Reviewer agent validates adherence to standards.

questions.question: What strategies do you use to reduce token costs and inference latency for enterprise conversational AI applications handling 100,000+ daily sessions?
questions.explanation: Discuss: Semantic caching of frequent responses, prompt compression, utilizing Small Language Models (SLMs) for routing, and response streaming.

questions.question: How does Capgemini prepare employees for the future of AI through the Capgemini University learning programs?
questions.explanation: Cover: Capgemini University certifications, prompt engineering bootcamps, responsible AI governance workshops, and hands-on client innovation labs.

questions.question: Capgemini is guided by 7 Core Values: Honesty, Boldness, Trust, Freedom, Fun, Modesty, and Team Spirit. Which of these values has influenced your engineering career most?
questions.explanation: Select one value (e.g. Boldness, Team Spirit, or Honesty), illustrate with a concrete academic or project example, and connect it to your professional growth.

questions.question: Why do you specifically choose Capgemini for your professional journey in technology consulting?
questions.explanation: Highlight: Capgemini's strong European engineering heritage, global innovation focus, commitment to sustainability, and collaborative multicultural work environment.

questions.question: Capgemini has major development centers across India (Mumbai, Pune, Bangalore, Hyderabad, Chennai, Kolkata). Are you fully flexible with relocation and project assignments?
questions.explanation: Affirm: Complete willingness to relocate, readiness to adapt to client project schedules, and enthusiasm for collaborating with international squads.

questions.question: Tell me about a time you demonstrated 'Boldness' by proposing an unconventional or innovative solution to solve a complex software challenge.
questions.explanation: Use STAR: Outline the traditional barrier, the bold innovative approach you proposed, how you convinced peers with data, and the successful outcome.

questions.question: How do you handle working in an agile project where requirements change unexpectedly right before a major sprint delivery?
questions.explanation: Showcase: Emotional stability, prioritizing customer requirements, collaborating with the scrum master, and adapting sprint deliverables pragmatically.

questions.question: Describe a time you received constructive feedback during a technical code review that required significant refactoring. How did you react?
questions.explanation: Emphasize: Modesty, gratitude for quality insights, separating personal ego from code quality, and implementing robust improvements.

questions.question: Tell me about a project where 'Team Spirit' was essential to overcoming an aggressive deadline or technical failure.
questions.explanation: Highlight: Mutual support, pair programming, helping a struggling teammate unblock their module, and celebrating success as one cohesive team.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself progressing at Capgemini over the next 3 to 5 years as a software engineer?
questions.explanation: Connect: Aspiring to grow from Software Engineer to Senior Software Engineer / Consultant, earning architectural certifications, and mentoring juniors.

questions.question: How do you maintain high personal ethics and 'Honesty' when reporting project progress or encountering software defects?
questions.explanation: Demonstrate: Transparent status reporting, never hiding known bugs, and communicating issues early so the team can address them collectively.

questions.question: Do you have any questions for Capgemini leadership regarding our digital practices, campus onboarding, or learning culture?
questions.explanation: Candidate asks about Capgemini Exceller development programs, opportunities to contribute to sustainability initiatives, or international projects.

questions.question:
Capgemini Pseudocode Analysis: What is the output of the following pseudocode?
Integer a = 5, b = 10, c = 2
a = (a + b) / c
If (a > 6)
    b = a * c
Else
    b = a - c
Print b [CAPGEMINI Version]
questions.explanation: a = (5 + 10) / 2 = 15 / 2 = 7 (integer division). Condition (a > 6) evaluates to (7 > 6) which is True. b = a * c = 7 * 2 = 14.

questions.question: Capgemini Game-Based Logic: In a grid path puzzle, a delivery token moves from (0,0) to (3,3). If cell (1,1) and cell (2,2) are blocked obstacles, how many valid shortest paths exist moving only Right and Down? [CAPGEMINI Version]
questions.explanation: Total unconstrained paths = C(6,3) = 20. Paths through (1,1) = C(2,1) * C(4,2) = 2 * 6 = 12. Subtracting blocked paths and accounting for overlap leaves 10 valid paths.

Integer z = (x & y) + (x | y)
Print z [CAPGEMINI Version]
questions.explanation: Mathematical identity for any integers: (x & y) + (x | y) = x + y. Here x + y = 9 + 5 = 14.

questions.question: A person completes a project in 18 days working 8 hours a day. In how many days can the same project be completed working 6 hours a day at the same pace? [CAPGEMINI Version]
questions.explanation: Total man-hours = 18 * 8 = 144 hours. At 6 hours/day: days = 144 / 6 = 24 days.

questions.question: How do Java 21 Virtual Threads (Project Loom) differ from traditional platform threads, and what is the underlying carrier thread model? [CAPGEMINI Spec]
questions.explanation: Platform threads wrap heavy 1-to-1 OS threads (~1MB stack). Virtual threads are lightweight user-mode threads managed by JVM (~few KB). When a virtual thread executes blocking I/O, JVM unmounts it from the ForkJoinPool carrier thread, freeing carrier threads for other work.

questions.explanation: Emphasize: Modesty, gratitude for quality insights, separating personal ego from code quality, and implementing robust improvements.

questions.question: Tell me about a project where 'Team Spirit' was essential to overcoming an aggressive deadline or technical failure. [CAPGEMINI Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Highlight: Mutual support, pair programming, helping a struggling teammate unblock their module, and celebrating success as one cohesive team.

questions.question: Where do you see yourself progressing at Capgemini over the next 3 to 5 years as a software engineer? [CAPGEMINI Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Connect: Aspiring to grow from Software Engineer to Senior Software Engineer / Consultant, earning architectural certifications, and mentoring juniors.

questions.question: How do you maintain high personal ethics and 'Honesty' when reporting project progress or encountering software defects? [CAPGEMINI Culture Dimension]
questions.explanation: Demonstrate: Transparent status reporting, never hiding known bugs, and communicating issues early so the team can address them collectively.

questions.question: Do you have any questions for Capgemini leadership regarding our digital practices, campus onboarding, or learning culture? [CAPGEMINI Culture Dimension]
